desc: A two-page memorandum dated 9 January 1953, reference G-1579-4, classified SECRET and unsigned, written by Battelle Memorial Institute's H. C. Cross to Miles E. Goll at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base under Project Stork. Jacques Vallee found it in 1967 among J. Allen Hynek's papers and, not then knowing the author's identity, gave him the codename 'Pentacle'. The memorandum recommends establishing controlled experiments in selected areas of the United States with high concentrations of UFO reports, using observation posts equipped for visual skywatch, radar and photography, and states that 'many different types of aerial activity should be secretly and purposefully scheduled within the area.' It was written five days before the CIA-convened Robertson Panel met on 14-16 January 1953 - the panel whose recommendations set the government's public debunking posture for the next fifteen years. Vallee's judgement, which this board records as the significant one, is that the Robertson Panel was never briefed on the Pentacle proposals, and that a separate body had already determined the boundaries of what the panel could consider. The memorandum is the founding document of the contractor-side manipulation thesis: it shows a private institute proposing, to its Air Force customer, to manufacture the stimulus that the official investigation would then be asked to explain. No signed original has ever been produced by the Air Force or by Battelle.
